taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Full-corpus review against VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.6 retains the occurrence as unclassified. VIGIL-FC-000048 Verification-Dependency Access Failure is the closest candidate. Fresh testimony materially strengthens four elements of that class: users had existing OpenAI accounts, some explicitly reported paid Plus entitlements; practical access depended on the Microsoft-linked authentication/token-exchange route; the route failed with repeated token_exchange_failed errors rather than establishing account invalidity; and affected users were unable to complete sign-in through that route. However, the fifth recognition condition is not established for the occurrence as a whole: the evidence does not show that no proportionate cached, grace, alternative-verification or degraded-access path remained available. At least one user retained smartphone access, while another reported that Google sign-in did not restore access to the affected account. VIGIL therefore does not convert heterogeneous fallback evidence into a canonical FC-000048 occurrence. VIGIL-FC-000032 Access-State Collapse is not established because OpenAI's status record specifically distinguishes the affected Microsoft personal-account route rather than collapsing it into a generic account state. VIGIL-FC-000031 Authentication-State Continuity Failure is not established because no expiry, revocation, refresh, recovery, replacement or reauthentication propagation defect is evidenced.

assessment_boundaries: The provider confirms the affected Microsoft-personal-account sign-in route but does not disclose internal root cause or allocate responsibility between OpenAI and Microsoft components.
The token_exchange_failed string is treated as an observed symptom of the federated sign-in path, not as proof of a particular backend implementation defect.
Paid-account testimony supports an otherwise-valid-entitlement candidate condition for Verification-Dependency Access Failure, but fallback availability differs across reports and is not generalised.
The incident is not classified merely because a third-party identity dependency caused access loss.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: OpenAI reported that users signing in with Microsoft personal accounts were unable to sign in, applied mitigation and reported full recovery on 5 June 2026. Multiple contemporaneous users reported token_exchange_failed errors on Microsoft-linked accounts, including paid Plus accounts. One report retained smartphone access despite web-browser failure; another reported that attempting Google sign-in did not restore access to the affected account.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence demonstrates why federated identity dependencies and fallback state must be represented separately from account validity. A failed identity route can block practical access to an otherwise existing account without implying suspension, revocation or entitlement loss. The governance question is therefore not merely whether sign-in failed, but whether a valid or unresolved entitlement remains practically reachable through a proportionate alternate path. The public evidence establishes the dependency failure but does not establish a uniform absence of such fallback across affected users.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: INC-000021 provides a useful near-boundary case for Verification-Dependency Access Failure. It shows that evidence of a paid entitlement plus failed federated verification can satisfy much of the class while still falling short if fallback availability is unresolved or heterogeneous. That boundary prevents VIGIL from treating every identity-provider outage as a verification-dependency governance failure.
